questions.question_text: What do the acronyms MSP and MRP stand for in market regulation?
options: A) Maximum Sales Price & Minimum Retail Price
B) Minimum Support Price & Maximum Retail Price
C) Marginal Supply Price & Market Retail Price
D) Minimum Storage Price & Maximum Revenue Price
questions.correct_answer: B) Minimum Support Price & Maximum Retail Price
questions.explanation: MSP is the floor price guaranteed by government to protect farmers; MRP is the upper price limit legally chargeable to retail consumers.

questions.question_text: The price at which the quantity demanded by buyers exactly equals the quantity supplied by sellers is called the ________ price.
questions.explanation: Equilibrium price balances market supply and demand vectors without surplus or shortage.

questions.question_text: True or False with Justification: Wholesalers sell products directly to end consumers in tiny individual quantities.
questions.correct_answer: False. Wholesalers purchase in large bulk from manufacturers and sell to retailers; retailers sell small quantities to end consumers.
questions.explanation: Wholesalers operate in bulk trade with commercial distributors, whereas retailers serve individual consumers.

questions.question_text: Trace the physical supply chain stages of cotton clothing from farmer to retail consumer.
questions.correct_answer: Raw Cotton Farmers -> Textile Mills -> Wholesale Warehouses -> Regional Distributors -> Retail Outlets -> Final Consumers.
questions.explanation: Value addition and bulk distribution occur step-by-step across agricultural, industrial, wholesale, and retail links.

questions.question_text: What quality assurance do the ISI mark, FSSAI logo, and BEE Star rating provide to consumers?
questions.correct_answer: ISI: Industrial product safety. FSSAI: Food safety and hygiene certification. BEE Star rating: Electrical appliance energy efficiency.
questions.explanation: Government certification marks verify safety compliance, hygienic standards, and energy performance.

questions.question_text: Why does the government establish Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for agricultural crops during bumper harvest seasons?
questions.correct_answer: Bumper harvests cause crop market gluts that drive open market prices down. MSP provides a guaranteed government price floor, purchasing crops to protect farmers against financial collapse.
questions.explanation: Price floors prevent distress sales by guaranteeing minimum farm gate returns during oversupply gluts.

questions.question_text: Case Study: During tomato harvest season, prices in Andhra Pradesh crash to ₹1/kg, causing farmers to dump crops on highways. Analyze why open market prices crashed and propose market infrastructure solutions.
questions.correct_answer: Cause: Extreme supply surplus exceeding immediate local retail demand. Solutions: Building cold storage warehouses, establishing local tomato processing factories (sauce/puree), and state transport to high-demand urban markets.
questions.explanation: Storage infrastructure and processing processing absorb seasonal crop gluts, maintaining stable market pricing.
